assertions.text: Part A: resolves the head SHA (gh pr view --json headRefOid) and the current actor (gh api user) after the PR is created
Part A: verifies live write/maintain/admin merge-capable permission before attesting
Part A: states the attestation marker is built via jq -n --arg (or equivalent), never by interpolating the reason directly into a shell string
Part A: states the bypass is SHA-bound and a new push invalidates it
Part B: states an empty-reason bypass is rejected before any comment or label action, and the already-created PR is unaffected
Part C: states a failed attestation (insufficient permission) is reported plainly as a failure, distinct from success, and that the PR itself still exists and is unaffected

Part A: names the specific repo-internal mechanism that actually enforces the SHA-binding — that check_bypass in scripts/marketplace_ci/review.py requires an exact head-SHA match — not just generic 'a new push changes the SHA so it stops matching' reasoning a security-savvy agent could invent without reading this repo's own code
